definition: The grammatical correctness and naturalness of generated text from a purely linguistic standpoint, independent of factual accuracy or relevance.
details: Fluency was a major challenge for earlier generation systems but has become largely solved by modern LLMs, shifting evaluation focus toward correctness, relevance, and reasoning quality instead.

explainer.lead: Fluency is whether generated text reads naturally and follows the rules of language. It matters because smooth writing can still be wrong or irrelevant, so fluency needs to be judged separately from the quality of the answer.

tiers.eli5: Fluency is like checking whether a sentence sounds like something a person would naturally say. "The cat sleeps on the mat" is fluent, while "Cat the mat sleeps" is not. But a smooth sentence can still be untrue, just as a clearly told story can still be made up.
tiers.practitioner: Use fluency as a separate evaluation criterion when assessing generated text, alongside correctness, relevance, and reasoning quality. Modern LLMs have largely addressed the fluency problems seen in earlier generation systems, so evaluation effort now usually focuses on those other criteria. Do not treat a natural-sounding output as evidence that it is accurate or useful.
tiers.paperLevel: Fluency(text) evaluates grammatical correctness and naturalness from a purely linguistic standpoint, independent of factual accuracy and relevance. Earlier generation systems often struggled with it, while modern LLMs have largely solved the problem. Its main limitation as an overall quality measure is that fluent text can still contain factual errors or fail to address the task.

explainer.example: "The cats sleeps on the mat" has a grammar problem, while "The cat sleeps on the mat" is fluent. "The moon is made entirely of green cheese" is also fluent, but it is factually false, showing why fluency alone is not enough.

usedIn.name: Large language model evaluation
usedIn.detail: Fluency checks whether generated responses are grammatical and natural, separately from their correctness.

usedIn.name: Text generation evaluation
usedIn.detail: It provides a linguistic quality check alongside relevance and factual accuracy.

usedIn.name: Machine translation evaluation
usedIn.detail: It distinguishes natural-sounding output from whether the translation is accurate or appropriate.

explainer.intuition: Fluency asks, "Does this read like natural, grammatical language?" rather than "Is it true?" or "Does it answer the question?"
howItWorks: Read the generated text on its linguistic merits.
Check whether its sentences are grammatically correct.
Check whether its wording and flow sound natural.
Judge factual accuracy and relevance separately.
explainer.whyItMatters: Separating fluency from other qualities makes evaluation clearer and prevents polished language from hiding mistakes. Because modern LLMs are largely fluent, evaluation can focus more on correctness, relevance, and reasoning quality.
misconceptions: Fluent text is not necessarily factually accurate.
Natural writing does not guarantee that the text is relevant to the task.
Fluency being largely solved in modern LLMs does not make overall evaluation solved.
